UrbanMart Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the UrbanMart Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss UrbanMart's results for the Q3. Joining me on today’s call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report UrbanMart's performance for the Q3. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover four key aspects of our performance:

1. Overall Performance: In Q3, we achieved comparable store sales growth of 3.2%, driven by a balanced mix of traffic recovery and basket expansion across our over 850 brick-and-mortar locations in 38 states. Total revenue came in strong at $2.82 billion, up 4.1% year-over-year, reflecting resilience in value-oriented general merchandise, apparel, home essentials, and seasonal goods amid cooling inflation and bifurcated consumer spending—essentials steady while discretionary faced headwinds from high interest rates and a softening housing market.

2. E-Commerce Growth: Digital channels are accelerating, with e-commerce now at 12% penetration, up from prior periods, fueled by 8-10% growth in buy-online-pick-up-in-store orders through RFID-enabled curbside in 200 high-density stores. Marketplace partnerships like Walmart Connect and Instacart added 15% year-over-year growth, while ship-from-store fulfillment hit 65% rates in key markets, seamlessly blending our physical footprint with online demand.

3. Store Performance: Our stores remain the core, driving 88% of sales, with regional variations highlighting our localized approach—Southeast leading at +5.8% comps on tourism and in-migration, offset by softer West Coast results. Remodels in 50 locations delivered +7% comp uplift via omnichannel hubs, and new small-format Urban Express stores in Sunbelt markets are optimizing traffic density over 1,200 visits per week.

4. Marketing Initiatives: We've ramped high-ROI digital marketing to 68% of spend, generating 4.8x ROAS through social, search, and retail media networks, while loyalty personalization via our app boosts repeat visits and basket size.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more details on our financial results.

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Mike. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.82 billion, a 4.1% increase compared to the same period last year, propelled by 3.2% comp-store sales growth on a 2-for-1 basis, including a 2.1% traffic increase and 1.0% average ticket uplift to around $52.

Gross margin was 28.7%, expanding 110 basis points year-over-year, primarily driven by favorable product mix toward private-label items now at 28% of sales—up 400 basis points—with markdowns contained to 22%, stable freight costs post-Red Sea issues, and shrink below 1.4% through Eagle Eye detection and computer vision in 50 stores.

Operating expenses were $649 million, representing 23.0% of revenue, benefiting from labor efficiencies via Crew Flex scheduling at 65% utilization and utility savings from LED retrofits and solar in Texas stores.

Net income was $182 million, or $0.87 per share.

We generated $360 million in cash flow from operations, underscoring our strong free cash flow conversion.

Inventory levels are currently well-controlled at about 12 weeks of supply, with turns improving to 5.2x, thanks to AI demand forecasting reducing stockouts by 25%.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

As we look deeper, let me unpack the regional performance variations, which were a key driver of our overall comps this quarter. While we delivered solid top-line results, our brick-and-mortar footprint across Northeast, Southeast, Midwest, and West showed meaningful dispersion, underscoring localized strategies like targeted remodels, omnichannel execution, and inventory optimization. Northeast, 25% of square footage and 28% of comps mix, posted +1.5% comps, lagging due to unseasonable weather suppressing seasonal apparel traffic—flat at +0.2%—though home goods rose +3.2% on private-label kitchen items with 4.1% AUR growth. We've accelerated Store 2.0 remodels in Boston and Philly, with 12 completions featuring RFID shrink reduction of 15% and BOPIS lockers lifting digital fulfillment 22%; early lifts +7.2% comps, and loyalty app personalization targets 45% penetration for +0.3 UPT. Southeast, 30% square footage and 32% comps, starred at +5.8% comps from Florida tourism and infrastructure stimulus, traffic +4.7%, conversion +80 bps to 29.2%; home improvement +9.1% on patio demand, apparel +6.4% beating Macy's peers. Margins up 150 bps to 39.5% via Savannah DC efficiencies; adding 18 small-format stores in Raleigh-Durham with 12% curbside sales, local supplier tie-ins lifting basket $4.20, set to drive 35% of FY comps. Midwest, 22% square footage and 21% comps, +2.1% amid farm income softness—traffic +1.8%, ticket -0.5% on durables trade-down—but footwear +4.5%; op ex down 2.2% via Workforce Optimizer cutting overtime 18%, inventory turns to 5.2x, and Essentials Hubs enabling same-day delivery boosting omnichannel +14% in Chicago tests. West Coast, 23% square footage and 19% comps, -0.5% from California inflation and e-comm pressure—traffic -1.2%, apparel -3.7%—but home +1.9% on sustainable lines; precision pricing via Flexport cut dwell 22%, 10 urban conversions with cafes lifting traffic +5.3%, ship-from-store at 65%. Across regions, comp dispersion tightened to 650 bps, with $250 million tech investment yielding 3.2x ROI; guiding regional comps +2.5% to +4.0% FY24, capex tilted to Southeast/Midwest growth, Northeast remodels, West tech for EBITDA to $1.15-$1.18 billion and ROIC 11.2%.

Shifting to marketing and advertising expense trends, these came in at $118 million for the quarter, or 4.2% of net sales—up 8 basis points YoY but flat sequentially. This disciplined reallocation targets high-ROI channels amid consumer confidence at 98.7, pressuring discretionary. Total spend grew 12% YoY, outpacing top-line, with digital at 68%—up from 55%—versus traditional media down 18% to 15%, ROAS 4.8x vs. 2.1x. Search/programmatic $54 million or 42%, up 22%, Google/Bing CPC $1.42 up 7% on home keywords; programmatic video lifted AOV $128 via loyalty app data from 28 million users +14% YoY. Social $32 million up 28%, TikTok/Meta campaigns like #UrbanMartHack generated 2.7 million UGC, 3.2x ROAS driving 18% e-comm sales; our Media Network piloted with P&G/Unilever for $8 million offsetting 6% spend. AI personalization with Salesforce/Adobe serves geo-fenced creatives, boosting Southeast traffic 22% via Clean Room attribution and Sensormatic counters. U.S. spend $92 million up 15% in Sun Belt holding +2.1% comps; Canada flat at CAD 18 million with YouTube Shorts 2.5x ROAS; Europe €12 million scaling in-store screens. CAC down 9% to $24, CLV $412 via BOPIS 42% transactions; sunset TV for CTV Hulu/Roku, DoorDash/Uber pilots at 5x ROAS. Q4 at 4.3-4.5% sales, digital to 72% with full-funnel attribution.

Before Q&A, let me provide forward-looking guidance for Q4 ending December 2024 and full FY2024, navigating 2.5% core CPI, resilient essentials, interest rate pressures. Q4 net sales $2.55-$2.65 billion, +4-7% YoY, comps 2.5-4.5% on holiday traffic +12-15% like Target Circle; gross margin 36.5-37.2% +20 bps on private-label 28% and Dallas DC freight -8%; SG&A 23.8-24.2% via AI labor to 65% stores -12% OT; EPS $1.25-$1.35, EBITDA $420-$450 million, FCF $300-$350 million for dividend/repurchases. Sunbelt 35% base +5-7% comps on housing +6%, 12 new stores; Midwest 2-4%; Northeast/West flat-+2% on rents $28/sq ft. FY2024 sales raised to $10.3-$10.5 billion +5-7%, comps 3-4%, EPS $4.60-$4.80 from prior, margins 36.8% on hardlines mix +150 bps, SG&A <24%. Capex $450 million +10% YoY for 50 remodels RFID 98% in-stock, BOPIS +22%; Rewards 18 million members 55% sales, AI offers +300 bps comps; 40% recycled private-label +4% eco sales. Risks: delayed Fed cuts >6.5% mortgages, Red Sea; upside Walmart Marketplace, DoorDash same-day.

Finally, the key assumptions underlying our guidance for Q4 and FY2025. We're guiding Q4 revenue $2.85-$2.92 billion, 2-4% SSS; FY25 $11.9-$12.2 billion, SSS 3-5%, adjusted EBITDA $1.05-$1.12 billion, gross margins 28.5-29.0% +40-60 bps. Assumes no macro shocks, stable FX, omnichannel efficiencies. Revenue: SSS from 1-2% traffic +1-2% ABS, October pilots +1.5% on Urban Value Days; AUR flat-+1%, UPT low-single via cross-merch, private-label 28% +400 bps margin. E-comm 14-16% sales, BOPIS +8-10%, marketplace +15%. Sq ft -1% drag 15 Northeast closures, offset 8 Urban Express Sunbelt; Southeast +5-7%, Midwest flat-+2%, West +1-3% vs. CA labor. Gross: mix to apparel/home +50 bps AI forecasting -25% stockouts, markdowns 22%, freight flat $3,500/FEU Vietnam/Mexico, shrink <1.4% Eagle Eye 70% stores +CV 15% ORC drop. SG&A 23.0-23.5% +50 bps delever, wages 3.5-4.0% Crew Flex 65%, occupancy 10.5% 2.5% escalations percentage rents, utilities $12M LED/solar. Capex $450-$500M: 40% remodels BOPIS, 30% Memphis DC AutoStore, 20% mobile POS, 10% maint +75 bps productivity. EBITDA 8.8-9.2%, tax 24%, repurchases $300M from $1.1B FCF. Sensitivities: 50 bps cut +100 bps SSS, 4% inflation -1% ABS; 65% traffic $50k-$100k value focus; tariffs mitigated 20% U.S. localization. Embeds barbell consumer, share gains via experiential stores/omnichannel/data ops; upper half if traffic holds.

We remain focused on execution. Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of softening housing market on your sales?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, John. Absolutely, the softening housing market has pressured discretionary home categories like decor and durables, contributing to some of the mix shift we saw, particularly in Midwest and West where big-ticket demand softened amid rates above 6.5%. That said, essentials and private-label home items held firm, with +3.2% in Northeast home goods offsetting via ForgeLine cookware. Our localized assortments and omnichannel—like BOPIS for quick pickups—have captured resilient remodel traffic, and Sunbelt in-migration supports +5-7% there. We're positioned well as housing normalizes.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Davis with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Davis (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Emily. For Q4, we're guiding comps to 2.5% to 4.5%, balancing holiday promotions like Black Friday Cyber Week tailwinds with cautious discretionary. Traffic assumes 1-2% uplift from Value Days events, basket from cross-merch and loyalty personalization. Regionally, Southeast accelerates to 5-7%, others moderate, with e-comm integration offsetting any pure-store softness. Upper end if Fed cuts materialize.

Operator:
Our next question is from David Lee with Morgan Stanley.

David Lee (Morgan Stanley):
Thanks. On marketing, how are you thinking about ROAS sustainability with rising CPCs?

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Good question, David. ROAS at 4.8x digital holds via first-party data from 28 million loyalty users and AI personalization shifting to high-efficiency channels like Meta Advantage+ and programmatic video. CPC up 7% is manageable with CAC down 9% overall, and retail media offsets via our network's $8 million pilot revenue. Q4 digital to 72% mix ensures leverage as we scale attribution.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes the Q&A portion.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, VP of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.

aspect_summary.Key assumptions underlying guidance: Assumes no macro shocks, stable FX, omnichannel efficiencies; Q4 SSS 2-4% from 1-2% traffic +1-2% ABS, e-comm 14-16%, private-label 28%; regional: Southeast +5-7%, Midwest flat-+2%, West +1-3%; gross margins 28.5-29.0% via mix/AI forecasting/low markdowns/shrink; SG&A 23.0-23.5%; capex $450-500M on remodels/DC/tech; EBITDA 8.8-9.2%; sensitivities to Fed cuts/inflation.
aspect_summary.Regional performance variations: Q3 comps: Southeast +5.8% (tourism/in-migration), Northeast +1.5% (weather), Midwest +2.1% (farm softness), West Coast -0.5% (inflation/e-comm); dispersion 650 bps; FY24 guide +2.5-4.0% regionally, capex tilted to Southeast/Midwest; Q4/FY25: Southeast +5-7%, Midwest 2-4%/flat-+2%, Northeast/West flat-+2%/+1-3%.
aspect_summary.Marketing and advertising expense trends: Q3: $118M (4.2% sales, +12% YoY, +8 bps), digital 68% (up from 55%, 4.8x ROAS), traditional -18%; search/programmatic 42%, social 28%; CAC -9%; Q4: 4.3-4.5% sales, digital 72% with full-funnel attribution and high-ROI channels like Meta/programmatic.
